title: Structured Tool Output Contract
context: The AURA 2.0 contract Phase 3 requires the tool system to be machine-readable end to end. Tool results were previously a bool plus free-form prose, so the reasoning layer could not distinguish capability absence from a crash or a timeout from a definite no-op. Provider-level function-calling failures collapsed into generic task-aborted messages that invited failover retries against incapable providers.
decision: tools/outcome.py defines four separate vocabularies - ToolStatus (SUCCESS/FAILED/PARTIAL/DENIED/UNAVAILABLE/INVALID_ARGUMENTS/TIMEOUT/CANCELLED/UNKNOWN), ToolError with a category derived from its code (CAPABILITY distinct from PROVIDER), Evidence with a tri-state verified flag, and SideEffect (READ_ONLY/IDEMPOTENT/NON_IDEMPOTENT/UNKNOWN). ToolResult gains status/error_code/evidence/execution identity and derives retryability from (status, side_effect); UNKNOWN is never truthy; malformed output is downgraded to UNKNOWN, not accepted; serialize_for_model renders fixed STATUS/TOOL/EVIDENCE/RETRY lines into the prompt; the registry exposes definitions() and MCP-adapted export_mcp() without making MCP a runtime dependency.
alternatives: A full JSON Schema library for validation
Making a real MCP server a runtime dependency
rejected_alternatives: Letting each tool write its own status/error prose
Reusing ToolRisk for retry safety (conflating permission with retry, the phantom-verification bug)
A single generic failed taxonomy without PARTIAL/DENIED/UNAVAILABLE/UNKNOWN
consequences: The reasoning layer can branch on status, error_category, evidence_state and retryability without parsing prose. Tool authors declare output_schema and side_effect on the class; the honest default is undeclared/UNKNOWN. Human-confirmation, permission and capability gates are untouched. Existing string-returning tools still work through the preserved legacy fields. One new per-execution diagnostics line carries identity/status/duration/retryability/evidence state, never arguments or content, and trace failure never breaks execution.
